keyVerseText: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.
rootMeaning: The Greek noun κόλπος (kólpos) is apparently a primary word with no known root derivation, indicating its fundamental nature in the language. Its core meaning centers on a hollow or fold, specifically the bosom or lap, suggesting an intimate, enveloping space. This literal sense extends metaphorically to natural hollows such as bays or creeks, emphasizing a protective or containing quality beyond the English gloss of 'bosom' alone.
usageInScripture: Across its six occurrences, κόλπος most frequently translates as 'bosom,' highlighting a close, intimate association, often figurative of protection or nearness. One instance translates as 'creek,' showing its application to natural hollows like bays. This range from personal, relational imagery to physical geographic features reveals the word's common theme of an embracing or enclosing space, whether human or natural.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding κόλπος as the bosom enriches our grasp of biblical imagery related to closeness, care, and provision, reflecting God's intimate relationship with His people. The word’s use for the bosom or lap conveys warmth and protection, reminding believers of the tender care of Christ and the Father. Its metaphorical extension to natural hollows also speaks to God’s sovereign control over creation and His ability to shelter His people. This term invites reflection on the spiritual security found in God’s embrace and the overflowing generosity He extends to His children.
keyVerseReflection: In Luke 6:38, the phrase 'running over, shall men give into your bosom' uses κόλπος to evoke the image of an overflowing, abundant receptacle. This word enriches the verse by portraying God's blessings as not only ample but intimately received and held close to the heart. It emphasizes that the generosity one shows will be returned in a deeply personal and overflowing way, underscoring the relational nature of divine provision.
